Q: What is the proper way of using JavaScript, jQuery and AJAX to avoid reaching CPU limits? A:

After chatting with Cross I think we've find the problem. He's creating and Android map which looks for GPS coord, and send them to a PHP script on a web server. The PHP script update the record of the vehicle with the lat and Long, using the id of the vehicle (it's a car tracker) to know which record must be updated. Then an other PHP script reads the database and, using JS, move a marker on a map. The problem came from the fact Cross was using a timer in the Android App to ask GPS position every 2 sec, but he was calling the web server inside a loop without "timer". So in pseudo code he had something like that:

  Every 2 sec, ask for GPS Location
  Do
      send Location to server
  Loop

So even if the GPS location was uptaded only every 2 sec, he was calling the web server at full speed in continous.... which explain the CPU overload. I suggest Cross to such a think

       Get GPS location every 2 sec
       Do
          if Location has changed
            send to server
          endif
       Loop

Q: Swift Package Manager stuck on loading screen forever A:

If Xcode SPM packages timing out? Here's a subtle gotcha 🧵

If your Swift packages resolve fine in terminal but Xcode hangs forever, check this:

The setup:

  • Your ~/.gitconfig has an insteadOf rule rewriting HTTPS → SSH

  • Your ~/.ssh/config specifies a non-standard port for your git server

The problem: Terminal git uses your system's SSH binary, which reads ~/.ssh/config. All good.

Xcode's SwiftPM uses its own built-in SSH transport (libgit2), which does not read ~/.ssh/config. It tries the default port, nobody answers, timeout.

The fix: Remove the insteadOf rule in ~/.gitconfig so Xcode sticks with HTTPS. Or ensure your packages reference URLs that don't get rewritten.

Lesson: Just because git clone works in terminal doesn't mean Xcode sees the same world. They use different SSH tooling under the hood.

Hope this saves someone a frustrating afternoon.

Q: Selecting polygons which shares a boundary with target polygon in python preferably using GeoPandas A:

Intersect the df with itself. Polygons sharing a boundary with get geometry type LineString, polygons touching at corners will get geometry point and polygons covering themselves will get geometry polygon. Select by type LineString:

import geopandas as gpd

df = gpd.read_file(r"my_square_grid.shp")
df["id"] = range(df.shape[0]) #Create a unique id for each polygon
 
#Plot the df and label with id column
ax = df.plot(figsize=(8, 8), color="lightblue", ec="blue")
_ = df.apply(lambda x: ax.annotate(xy=(x.geometry.centroid.x, x.geometry.centroid.y),
                               text=x.id, fontsize=14, color="blue"), axis=1)

#Intersect the df with itself
df_inter = gpd.overlay(df, df, "intersection", False)

#Select the rows where the ids are different and the resulting geometry type is linestring
df_inter = df_inter.loc[(df_inter["id_1"]!=df_inter["id_2"]) & (df_inter.geometry.geom_type=="LineString")]

#Save each grids neighbouring ids as a list in "neighbors" column
df["neighbors"] = df["id"].map(df_inter.groupby("id_1")["id_2"].agg(lambda x: list(x)).to_dict())

#Print grid no 5:s neighbors
#print(df.loc[df["id"]==5]["neighbors"].iloc[0])
#[1, 4, 6, 9]

#Annotate the plot with the neighbors column
_ = df.apply(lambda x: ax.annotate(xy=(x.geometry.centroid.x-700, x.geometry.centroid.y-1200),
                                   text=f"Neighbors:\n{x.neighbors}", color="black", fontsize=8), axis=1)
